name: ac-coverage
why:
The C3 half of verify: map each AC to evidence, in the framework's own verdict vocabulary. AC-1 has implementation and a robust test. AC-2 is implemented but no test asserts the log — the rubric's NO TEST. AC-3 is neither implemented nor tested — NO IMPL.

The distinction that matters is AC-2: a model that reads the diff as 'the feature was built' and stops will call it PASS, which is an audit signing off untested code while reporting coverage. That is the exact silent failure the AC audit exists to prevent.

Revised 2026-09-20. The first version invented labels (COVERED / IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED / MISSING) that appear nowhere in the framework, and the rig sent the agent body without its autoloaded ac-audit-rubric — so models were scored for failing to guess a vocabulary they had never been shown. Both are fixed; this probe now asks for the shipped verdicts and the rig supplies the rubric that defines them.

AC-1 accepts PASS or WEAK, 2026-09-20. Three models independently returned WEAK, and the rubric's own naive-shortcut check backs them: `return null;` would satisfy `expect(await repo.getById('x'), isNull)`, so the test is weak even though the implementation is right. The key said PASS. Second time on this rig that independent models rejecting an answer meant the answer was wrong.

Underspecification fixed, 2026-09-20 (third time on this probe set). AC-3 is keyed NO_IMPL, but the fixture showed only a diff hunk — so a model could not rule out retry logic living elsewhere, and 10 runs answered NO_TEST rather than assert absence from partial evidence. That was correct caution, not error. The fixture now states that the implementation shown is complete. Recurring lesson: when models disagree with this rig's key, the key has been wrong every time so far.
format:
Assign one verdict per criterion from the rubric's five. Respond with ONLY these three lines and nothing else:
AC-1: <PASS|WEAK|INCOMPLETE|NO_TEST|NO_IMPL>
AC-2: <PASS|WEAK|INCOMPLETE|NO_TEST|NO_IMPL>
AC-3: <PASS|WEAK|INCOMPLETE|NO_TEST|NO_IMPL>
